name: MAIN MERAH
description: Main Merah (Indonesian for 'Playing Red') is a traditional fishing card game popular in Indonesia. It is a variant of the broader 'Fishing' family (like Scopa or Kou-Shuu) but with a specific focus on color. In this game, only the RED cards (Hearts and Diamonds) have point value, leading to a unique secondary economy where players prioritize capturing red cards while using black cards as purely functional tools.

content.text: Main Merah (Indonesian for 'Playing Red') is a traditional fishing card game popular in Indonesia. It is a variant of the broader 'Fishing' family (like Scopa or Kou-Shuu) but with a specific focus on color. In this game, only the RED cards (Hearts and Diamonds) have point value, leading to a unique secondary economy where players prioritize capturing red cards while using black cards as purely functional tools.
Likely brought to the Indonesian archipelago by Portuguese or Dutch traders, the game evolved into its modern 'Red focus' in the 20th century.
2 players (10 cards each) or 3 players (7 cards each).
2 players: 10 cards each; 3 players: 7 cards each.

items.text: Two players: 10 cards each, 12 on table, 20 in draw pile. Standard setup.
Three players: 7 cards each, 10 on table, 21 in draw pile. First deal: dealer plays first; subsequently player with worst score in previous deal plays first.
Table sweep bonus: In many Indonesian house rules, clearing the table entirely (taking the last cards) grants a point bonus.
